beats.narration_text: Someone assumed datapack-builder would calculate their financials, the way an analyst would. It doesn't — it extracts and standardizes data from your sources into one workbook. Does datapack-builder extract my financials for me?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is datapack-builder. Its SKILL.md holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then acts on it. The file is the program.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, one after another, unless a step itself says to branch.

production_viz.label: ONE STEP AT A TIME
production_viz.caption: no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: datapack-builder's job is specific: pull financial data from CIMs, offering memos, SEC filings, web search, or MCP servers, and standardize it into one investment-committee-ready Excel workbook — consistent structure, proper formatting, assumptions documented. It's built for M&A due diligence and portfolio reporting, not for running the calculations itself or reworking a data pack that's already finished. What isn't in the SKILL.md's steps isn't part of the job.
datapack-builder doesn't calculate your numbers — it extracts and standardizes them into one workbook, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Paste this into Claude: 'I want to build a financial services data pack from a CIM, an offering memorandum, and SEC filings for an investment committee review. Read the datapack-builder skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it.' That last clause matters — asking Claude to explain first surfaces the actual steps it's about to run.
